verdict_reason: ONE low finding introduced by the R3 extension: the cycle half of unresolvedDependencyNote reports a cycle whose members no longer block, so the model-facing status line claims an unresolved dependency for a task the scheduler will dispatch. Everything else in the repair is verified: all seven round-1 findings are closed, every reading reproduced, both semantic reverts redden the right assertions, and the registry family is green end-to-end at the current revision.

findings.problem: The T-29 cycle extension reports a cycle without checking whether its members still block. Measured for T with deps ['B'] where B<->C cycle: with B and C both `failed` (or both `completed`), dependencyStates(T).blocking is [] — the task is CLAIMABLE, per OPT-1 'a FAILED dependency does not block' — yet unresolvedDependencyNote(T) returns ' [unresolved dep: cycle B\u2192C\u2192B]', and renderStatus appends that note to EVERY task line (lib/tools.js task-line template). So the model-facing status tells a reader that a dispatchable task has an unresolved dependency. A mutual pair of FAILED tasks is a natural record shape; the completed variant is reachable by force-completion, the family T-79 replays.
findings.requiredFix: Derive the cycle report from the same predicate the gate uses — report a cycle only while its members are still unsatisfied/non-terminal (e.g. skip cycle members whose status is terminal), or suppress the note when the task's own blocking set is empty. One condition, not a redesign; the phantom half is correct and unaffected.

observations.note: transitive deadlock is not named: with T deps ['A'] and A -> B -> C -> B, A is named ('cycle B→C→B') but T's note is empty although T can never be woken. The acceptance's observable is satisfied for every case it names (a nonexistent id, or a cycle through a dependency); naming T needs a reachability fixpoint, which the frozen row does not ask for.

both of the repair's 'before' sides are runs against git HEAD (pre-wave-2b), so they redden for a broader reason than the repaired line (its 6 failures include R7-era absences). My ARM F (count-only revert of just the name match) reddens exactly the 4 R5/R6 assertions, and ARM B (cycle half reverted) exactly the 4 cycle assertions — the sharper reds, recorded here.
